checks.title: Invoice ID must be unique
checks.rationale: The 'invoice_id' serves as the primary key for the dataset. Duplicates would indicate severe data integrity issues or transaction errors.
checks.assumption: The 'invoice_id' column is intended to be the unique identifier for each invoice record.

checks.title: Invoice ID must match expected pattern (INV_###)
checks.rationale: Enforcing a consistent pattern helps ensure that IDs are generated correctly and prevents accidental inclusion of non-standard identifiers.
checks.assumption: Invoice IDs follow a standard internal format, likely starting with 'INV_' followed by digits, as suggested by the pattern samples (AAA_999) and examples.

checks.title: GST Number must be present
checks.rationale: GST numbers are crucial for tax reporting and compliance in jurisdictions where GST applies. Missing values severely compromise the validity of the invoice record.
checks.assumption: The GST number is a mandatory field for all invoices recorded in this system, especially given the high frequency of 'IN' (India) country codes.

checks.title: GST Number must adhere to standard 15-character format
checks.rationale: Validating the structure of the GST number (GSTIN) ensures that the tax ID is correctly recorded, preventing downstream tax calculation or filing errors.
checks.assumption: The primary tax ID used is the Indian GSTIN, which is a 15-character alphanumeric code starting with a 2-digit state code.

checks.title: Amount must not be excessively negative
checks.rationale: While negative amounts represent credits or refunds, extremely large negative values often indicate data entry errors or system malfunctions.
checks.assumption: The maximum expected refund or credit amount is limited to a reasonable threshold (e.g., -10000.0).

checks.title: Amount must not exceed typical maximum invoice value
checks.rationale: Extremely high positive amounts could indicate fraud, data corruption, or a misplaced decimal point, requiring immediate review.
checks.assumption: Typical invoice amounts for this business rarely exceed 50,000.0 units of currency.

checks.title: Detect statistical outliers in invoice amounts
checks.rationale: Identifying amounts that are statistically unusual compared to the rest of the dataset helps flag potentially erroneous or exceptional transactions for manual review.
checks.assumption: Invoice amounts generally follow a predictable distribution, and significant deviations are worth investigating.

checks.title: Country code must be exactly 2 characters (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2)
checks.rationale: Standardizing country codes to the 2-character format ensures consistency for geo-mapping and reporting purposes.
checks.assumption: All country codes used in this dataset adhere to the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard.

checks.title: Monitor for new country codes
checks.rationale: New country codes might indicate business expansion into new markets or, more commonly, data entry errors if the list of supported countries is static.
checks.assumption: The set of valid countries is relatively stable, and sudden introduction of new codes should be flagged.

checks.title: GST Number must be 15 characters long
checks.rationale: The standard GSTIN format is 15 characters. Inconsistent lengths suggest incomplete or corrupted data entry.
checks.assumption: All valid GST numbers in this dataset must be 15 characters long.

checks.title: GST Number required if Country is 'IN'
checks.rationale: If an invoice is issued in India ('IN'), a GST number is typically required for tax compliance and input tax credit claims.
checks.assumption: Invoices originating from or destined for India (Country='IN') must have a non-null 'gst_number'.

checks.title: Invoice ID must maintain strict length of 7 characters
checks.rationale: The profile shows a strict length of 7 characters for all observed IDs. Maintaining this consistency prevents truncation or unexpected padding.
checks.assumption: The invoice ID generation system always produces 7-character strings.
